summary: Introductory PLG quickstart discovery. Astera interested in Redwood hosted API for rapid prototyping but evaluating Dedicated/Private for production due to data residency and compliance. Key concerns: time-to-first-token, free credits for proof-of-concept, SOC2/KMS, VPC connectivity, latency vs cost. Agreed next steps: send quickstart + credits, schedule technical demo/benchmark, share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Diego from my team will jump in on the tech stuff. Lina, thanks for taking time.
[00:12] Lina Park: Thanks, Maya. Quick context, we're exploring LLM features for our customer support routing and docs summarization, goal is POC in 3–4 weeks.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Perfect. High-level, Redwood has a PLG quickstart — you can sign up, get free credits, and call the hosted API within minutes. Time-to-first-token is usually under a minute if you use the quickstart flow.
[00:39] Emily Zhao: That's good. We're big on measuring time-to-first-token — our PM org hates waiting for infra. How does the quickstart work?
[00:45] Maya Chen: You sign up, get an API key, run a one-line curl or SDK call. We hand out starter credits, sandbox models, and sample prompt sets. I'll share the quickstart link after the call.
[00:58] Raj Patel: For POC we need to know cost estimates — ephemeral hosted pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity?
[01:05] Diego Ruiz: Right, hosted is usage-based per token. For heavy steady throughput Dedicated gives predictable unit cost with reserved GPU pools. For your POC, hosted + credits is fine; we'll look at Dedicated if you see stable QPS.
[01:22] Lina Park: Data residency: our contracts require logs not leave EU region. Does Redwood hosted support region pinning?
[01:30] Maya Chen: Yes, we have regional endpoints. For stricter controls we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) where you manage the network and keys. We also support KMS integrations for customer-managed keys.
[01:45] Lina Park: Are you SOC 2 certified? Our security team will ask.
[01:50] Maya Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II. I'll send the attestation and security whitepaper.
[01:56] Emily Zhao: Any gotchas with the SDK? We use Python and Node.
[02:02] Diego Ruiz: Official SDKs for both, simple wrappers. For streaming responses and function/tool calling we have examples. Some model-specific params differ, but quickstart covers that.
[02:14] Raj Patel: For production we need RBAC and SSO — SAML support?
[02:18] Maya Chen: Yes, enterprise accounts support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC. Private deployments also integrate with your identity provider.
[02:27] Lina Park: On latency — our load is mostly sub-second for small responses. What latency SLOs can we expect on hosted?
[02:35] Diego Ruiz: Median token latency depends on model and sequence length; for the smaller open models we often see tail latencies within our SLO at 95th percentile under 300–400ms for single-token steps. For strict low-latency we recommend routing or Dedicated with pinned capacity.
[02:52] Emily Zhao: What's the difference in engineering effort if we go Dedicated vs Private?
[02:57] Diego Ruiz: Dedicated is managed by Redwood but reserved to you — little operational footprint on your side. Private requires more setup: VPC peering or on-prem deployment, key management, and network ops. We provide deployment docs and a partner option if you need hands-on.
[03:12] Lina Park: For the POC we probably want hosted. Can you share limits and burst capacity?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Default hosted quota is modest; we can increase limits for POCs. There's also burst capacity lanes for spikes. We'll note your expected traffic so we can pre-warm.
[03:27] Raj Patel: How does caching and batching work? We run many short prompts and want cost efficiency.
[03:33] Diego Ruiz: We support automatic prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. For short prompts caching can reduce repeated token costs; batching helps throughput. We can suggest batching windows based on your latency targets.
[03:47] Emily Zhao: Any differences in model catalog between hosted and Private?
[03:50] Maya Chen: Hosted has our curated catalog and verified performance profiles. Private supports bringing down the same model variants and quantization profiles; only difference is image/firmware compatibility on very old hardware.
[03:59] Lina Park: Security question — audit logs retention and access controls?
[04:03] Maya Chen: Audit logs are available; retention depends on plan. Enterprise/Private can push logs to your storage and use KMS/HSM for encryption.
[04:13] Raj Patel: For the benchmark we want to run 1000 requests at 5 QPS and measure latency/cost. Can Diego help design that?
[04:20] Diego Ruiz: Absolutely. I'll put together a benchmark checklist: prompt set, expected sequences, measurement points, and model variants to test.
[04:28] Lina Park: Pricing — any discounts for committed usage?
[04:32] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated/reserved capacity has commit pricing. Hosted is standard usage-based but we can provide credits for pilots.
[04:40] Emily Zhao: How do you handle graceful degradation if capacity is constrained? We need fallbacks.
[04:46] Diego Ruiz: Smart routing: we can fallback to compatible model variants or route to another region or degraded latency tier. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies.
[05:00] Lina Park: What about observability — per-route token cost breakdown?
[05:04] Maya Chen: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing and error analysis. We can show a demo.
[05:12] Raj Patel: For the POC we want to limit data retention to 7 days. Is that configurable?
[05:17] Maya Chen: Hosted has default retention policies; we can configure retention and purge settings for enterprise accounts or Private.
[05:25] Emily Zhao: Do you support function calling for downstream tool integration?
[05:29] Diego Ruiz: Yes, structured output and function/tool calling are supported in the SDK.
[05:33] Lina Park: Any regulatory compliance options for EU customers?
[05:36] Maya Chen: We support region pinning, data residency, SOC2, and can discuss specific compliance packages.
[05:42] Raj Patel: What about keys — can we bring our own KMS?
[05:46] Maya Chen: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported on Private and enterprise tiers.
[05:50] Emily Zhao: How long to get us from signup to tokens live?
[05:53] Maya Chen: With quickstart it's minutes; if you need SSO or enterprise onboarding it can take days. For your POC hosted with credits is fastest.
[06:00] Lina Park: Is there a self-serve quota increase path?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Yes, self-serve for modest increases; for larger increases we coordinate via AE to adjust limits.
[06:10] Raj Patel: Any hidden latency on cold start for larger models?
[06:13] Diego Ruiz: Larger models can have cold-start overheads; we mitigate via pre-warming and KV cache. Also compilation/kernel selection affects initial steps.
[06:25] Emily Zhao: For the POC we want to try embeddings for search. Are embeddings billed differently?
[06:29] Maya Chen: Embeddings are billed per embedding unit, separate from generation tokens. We'll include sample cost estimates.
[06:34] Lina Park: Let's talk timeline: POC in 3–4 weeks, then evaluate Dedicated in next quarter.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll get the quickstart and credits sent, Diego will prep benchmarks, Raj will share infra details.
[06:48] Raj Patel: Any performance guarantees on Dedicated?
[06:51] Diego Ruiz: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on commitment.
[06:57] Emily Zhao: For the quickstart, can we add additional team members to the account?
[07:00] Maya Chen: Yes, team invites are supported; for enterprise-level governance we'll enable SSO and RBAC.
[07:07] Lina Park: Okay, can you send a sample contract or MSA for review?
[07:11] Maya Chen: We can send a redline-friendly MSA; typically after we have a pilot scope we provide one.
[07:17] Emily Zhao: Any limitations with the SDK in air-gapped setups?
[07:21] Diego Ruiz: For air-gapped you typically use our Private on-prem package; there are some ops steps but SDKs work locally.
[07:28] Maya Chen: I'll share links: quickstart guide (https://docs.redwood.com/quickstart), free credits request form, and security whitepaper.
[07:35] Raj Patel: Can you also include sample prompts and a cost calc spreadsheet?
[07:38] Diego Ruiz: Yes, we'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet and suggested prompts.
[07:42] Lina Park: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
[07:45] Emily Zhao: I think Raj will confirm infra; otherwise looks doable.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Great — recap: I'll send quickstart + credits + SOC2 and security doc; Diego will schedule the benchmark demo and share checklist; Raj will send infra details.
[07:58] Lina Park: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the POC.
[08:02] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up by email with artifacts and set up the demo.
